newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run little talked,Russian fuel rarer.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run little talked,Russian fuel rarer.

text.p: Little straight-run fuel oil changed hands in Europe on Tuesday, but the scarcity of Russian cargoes was holding their value in the north, traders said.
Low sulphur cargoes were little discussed in generally quiet trade, with prices at $96/$98 fob NWE. The last deal seen was on Friday from an Irish refiner into Britain at $96.75 fob.

Most attention was on Russian material. But there were no E-4s or M40s on offer, confirming the dwindling of supplies seen in the last month and which some traders blame on exporters' reluctance to ship out with prices so low.
Two M100s were on offer. One high water cargo aboard the Zoya, was offered around two means plus $3 and bid at two means flat or plus $1 cif.
The other cargo was being offered fob Tallin at around two means minus $3 or $4.
More plentiful supplies in the Mediterranean has pushed some straight-run towards the bunker market, with one M40 heading into Trieste on Friday.
At least two M100s and two M40s were available in the Black sea in the first half of May, traders added.
